text: I'm Rama Raihan, a full-stack developer from Salatiga, a small city in the hills of Central Java, Indonesia. I build and run web apps in Laravel and Next.js.
Lately I've been building AI apps: RAG, agents, chatbots and workflow automation.
My AI apps default to a local model through Ollama, so anyone can run them without an API key.
I deploy my own apps with Docker and Coolify on a VPS. GitHub Actions runs the checks on every push.
I care most about the parts that fail quietly, like a payment callback that lands while the app is down, or a backup nobody has ever restored.
Most of my client work lives in private repos, so it doesn't show up on GitHub.
I work from Salatiga on UTC+7, and I'm happy to work remotely with a team anywhere.
docs-rag-assistant: ask questions about your own PDFs, Word files and Markdown notes, in English or Indonesian. Every answer cites the file and page it came from.

Upload a file, it gets chunked and embedded into pgvector, and the answer streams back with page citations. In a small eval the right page came first for 16 of 16 questions, and all 3 off-topic ones were refused.
research-agent: a LangGraph agent that plans the research, waits for you to approve the plan, then searches the web, runs extra rounds when it finds gaps, and writes a cited report.

shop-support-bot: a support chatbot for a small coffee bean shop, on the web and in Telegram. It answers from the shop's policies, checks orders and stock, opens tickets, and hands the chat to a person when needed.
llm-gateway: one OpenAI-compatible endpoint in front of OpenAI, Gemini, Anthropic and Ollama, with fallback, retries, rate limits, an exact-match cache, hashed API keys and cost logs.
invoice-flow: a Laravel app that reads Indonesian supplier invoices with an LLM, checks the math, PPN and NPWP, and holds them for review before export.
text-to-sql-chat: ask a sales database questions in English or Bahasa Indonesia and get the SQL, the rows and a chart, with guardrails on the generated SQL. It also ships an MCP server.
issue-triage-action: a GitHub Action that labels new issues, flags likely duplicates and asks for missing details in one comment.
local-ai-coding-setup: my fully local AI coding setup on a laptop with a 6 GB RTX 3060. A coding agent in the terminal and autocomplete in VS Code.

antre: queue and booking for small clinics and barbershops. Book a slot with a Midtrans deposit or take a walk-in ticket. Staff call the next number, and a TV in the waiting room reads it out in Indonesian. Two counters never get the same ticket.
warung-pos: a point of sale for a small shop that keeps selling when the internet drops. Sales wait in an outbox on the device and sync later, and a retry never counts a sale twice.

webhook-inbox: a small Rust service that receives webhooks from Midtrans, Xendit and GitHub, checks the signature, stores every delivery and forwards it with retries, so a payment callback isn't lost while the app is down.
pg-backup: a Go tool that streams encrypted Postgres backups to S3-compatible storage, then proves each one by restoring it into a scratch database and checking the row counts.

project-clipper turns a long video into vertical clips for my YouTube channel: faster-whisper transcribes, Gemini picks the highlights, OpenCV tracks faces and ffmpeg burns in subtitles. Then it uploads them through the YouTube Data API.
ralaex is the household finance app my wife and I log our spending in. Budgets with alerts, receipt photos, charts and exports.
chaBubbleTwitch is a free Twitch chat overlay for OBS that shows chat as wooden speech bubbles, with Twitch emotes.
Next.js: most of my apps run on it. App Router, server components, the usual setup.
React for building the interface. Components, hooks, client state.
All my frontend and Node code is TypeScript now. It catches my mistakes before they reach the browser.
Tailwind CSS for styling. Quicker for me than keeping a separate stylesheet in sync.
Vite bundles the frontend assets on my Laravel projects.
Laravel for APIs, Eloquent, queues and auth. Blade when a page is better rendered on the server.
PHP is the language behind all the Laravel work.
Node.js runs the server side of Next.js, route handlers and server actions.
Python is the backend for my AI projects, managed with uv.
Go and Rust for small tools that ship as one binary. pg-backup is Go, webhook-inbox is Rust.
PHPUnit and Pest on the Laravel side, feature tests more than unit tests. Vitest and pytest in the TypeScript and Python projects.
Midtrans handles checkout and payments on the Indonesian projects.
PostgreSQL is my default. Relational data, migrations, a bit of PL/pgSQL when a query gets hairy.
MySQL is what most of my Laravel projects sit on, especially the ones on shared hosting.
MongoDB on an LMS, where the shape of the content kept changing.
pgvector does vector search inside Postgres, so there's no separate vector database to run.
Docker, so the app behaves the same on my laptop as it does on the server.
GitHub Actions runs lint and tests on every push, and deploys this site to GitHub Pages.
Coolify deploys my Laravel and Next.js apps to my own VPS instead of renting a platform.
Git for version control, one branch per feature.
FastAPI serves my docs assistant and research agent, with answers streamed over server-sent events.
LangGraph runs my research agent: a plan, a human review step, then parallel searches.
LlamaIndex does document ingestion and pgvector search in my docs question-answering app.
The Vercel AI SDK streams chat and tool calls in a Next.js support bot.
Prism PHP reads supplier invoices into typed data inside a Laravel app.
Ollama and llama.cpp for local models. I code with llama.cpp on my laptop.
One setting switches between the OpenAI, Gemini and Claude APIs in each of my AI apps.
MCP exposes the guarded SQL tools of text-to-sql-chat to Claude Desktop and Cursor.
